method.protocol: Playwright drove the real DSH web UI. The test used a real hosted DeepSeek chat completion for the first render, then exercised the host action path with real browser clicks.
method.secondTurn: The first automatic [iui-action] turn returned prose only. Per the pre-registered smoke protocol, the host then sent the exact complete replacement ops as a user message; the model called render_iui and the replacement rendered.
method.invalidOp: The invalid-op guard intentionally sent an ops array without an answer envelope and with an unknown component type. The model refused to call the tool; no invalid tool row was created. The prior valid interface remained usable.
method.secretHandling: The API key was supplied through DEEPSEEK_API_KEY in an ignored local environment file. No key or route token is included in this evidence.

checks.detail: render_iui tool row rendered the table and stats/tabs.
save_note action was declared by the render_iui envelope and appeared in the toolview.
Reversible save_note opened the host confirmation dialog.
Cancel closed the dialog without writing localStorage and without a new tool row.
Confirm wrote one note and sent an [iui-action] message.
The model answered the [iui-action] turn in prose, so the host re-sent the exact complete replacement; the second interface rendered with copy_text.
The model refused the deliberately invalid ops before calling the tool. The previous valid interface stayed available; this was not a tool-row validation cycle.
A usable copy_text action remained at the end.
No browser console or page error was recorded.

caveats: This is one model, one session, and one DSH web route; it is not a statistical model evaluation.

The automatic [iui-action] turn was prose-only. The acceptance uses the pre-registered exact complete-ops recovery, so it verifies the host update path but not autonomous second-turn model compliance.

The deliberately invalid ops were refused by the model before the tool call. A separate model that sends invalid JSON to render_iui would exercise the validator branch; the DSH protocol tests cover that branch without a model.
Screenshots and session records remain local and ignored; the repository contains no credential, token, screenshot, or session file.
